source.title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
source.authors: Sean McLeish; Ang Li; John Kirchenbauer; Dayal Singh Kalra; B. Bartoldson; B. Kailkhura; Avi Schwarzschild; Jonas Geiping; Tom Goldstein; Micah Goldblum

record.file_problem: No apparent text problem; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses Kaplan et al.'s FLOPs approximation for fixed-depth transformers (FLOPs = 6ND) to account for training cost, but does not test the scaling-law claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training and validation loss under initialization, optimizer, and recurrence-schedule comparisons, plus benchmark accuracy over compute. These results do not test power-law loss scaling, extrapolation, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or the other claim versions. It cites the 6ND FLOPs approximation for cost accounting; cited scaling-law results are not new results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study converts pretrained 1B models into depth-recurrent models and compares initialization, recurrence curricula, optimizers, layer selection and data mixtures. It uses Kaplan et al.'s 6ND FLOPs approximation only for cost accounting. It fits no power law across parameters, tokens or compute, runs no compute-optimal sweep, and tests no extrapolation. The one log-log extrapolation (Appendix Fig. 9) projects where two training-loss curves would cross, about 950B tokens. That is a convenience projection, not a test of V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors find that pretrained initialization, a recurrence curriculum and a healing data phase make retrofitted depth-recurrent models efficient. These models beat non-recurrent post-training on GSM8K/MATH per training FLOP while keeping general benchmark performance. They note experiments are at roughly 1B parameters and 50B tokens, so generalisation to larger scales is unverified.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or test the original scaling-law measurement; it uses Kaplan et al.'s FLOPs approximation for cost accounting.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that loss or performance changes with initialization, optimizer, recurrence schedule, training data, and layer selection; these comparisons do not establish sensitivity of fitted scaling-law exponents.

fits_no_version.finding: For Llama-initialized (2,4,2) recurrent models, linearly scheduling mean recurrence improves validation-loss efficiency per training FLOP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A recurrence-depth curriculum improves loss-per-FLOP efficiency in continued training of depth-recurrent models.

record.problems: No scaling-law sweep, power-law fits, or small-to-large extrapolation test is reported. The authors state that experiments are at the 1B parameter and 50B token scales and that generalisation to much larger scales requires further study. The relevant validation-loss comparison is presented as a figure without tabulated values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Other loss and benchmark results, including initialization and optimizer comparisons, concern recurrence-model training rather than the claim's scaling relationships and were not extracted as claim-bearing rows.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No test of small-run fits predicting larger runs. The Fig. 9 curve-crossing projection is not validated against any run.
Layer-selection and shape ablations (Figs. 12–15) change parameter counts and FLOPs. They are not fixed-parameter depth/width comparisons.
No power-law tests for other modalities or regimes, including continued training.
Benchmark accuracy is reported versus training FLOPs and test recurrence. No predictability relation with scale or loss is fitted or tested.
No analysis of exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test classification is confirmed. The study cites Kaplan et al. only for the FLOPs approximation. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit of held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No test of whether fits from smaller runs predict larger runs.
No sweep for loss-minimising parameter and token allocations across compute budgets.
Architecture and layer-selection comparisons are not tests of loss changes at fixed parameter count across depth and width.
No power-law tests in other modalities or the listed alternative training regimes.
Benchmark performance is measured during recurrence experiments, not tested for predictable improvement with scale or pretraining loss.
No analysis of scaling-law exponents, fit choices, or departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: Llama-initialized (2, 4, 2) depth-recurrent models
rows.operation_detail: Compared recurrence-depth schedules and measured validation loss over training steps and FLOPs.

conditions.value: Linearly scheduled mean recurrence versus other schedules, including no curriculum

rows.note: The text says linear scheduling has a small positive impact on validation loss as a function of steps and improves loss efficiency as a function of FLOPs. This is a schedule comparison, not a power-law scaling test.
rows.check: Recurrence-schedule comparison of validation loss (Fig. 3). It is not a scaling-law measurement and bears on no version. Values are figure-only. The subject is correct: a Llama-3.2-1B-initialized (2,4,2) model.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 3; Section 4.1 identifies Llama-3.2-1B initialization and FineWeb-Edu data.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 3; Section 4.1 identifies Llama-3.2-1B initialization and FineWeb-Edu data.

relation.reason: Applies the FLOPs approximation while evaluating its own retrofitting method, without testing the claimed power-law relationships.

tranche.reason: Uses Kaplan et al.'s 6ND approximation for training-cost accounting; the recurrence-schedule comparison does not test a listed scaling-law version.

source_check.notes: Figure 3 reports validation loss on one million tokens every 1000 training steps; numerical outcome values are figure-only. Appendix C.1 extrapolates training curves for initialization comparisons, without validating predictions on larger models.
